item.title: The AI Agent Framework Landscape
item.description:
Simple definition#

An agent framework is a library or SDK that implements the plumbing every agent needs — the loop that calls the model, executes tools and feeds results back — plus state, memory, multi-agent coordination, human-in-the-loop, guardrails and tracing. You write the instructions, tools and business logic; the framework runs them.

item.title: Python and TypeScript Agent Frameworks
item.description:
How to read this page#

Each profile answers the same questions: what is the core idea, what does minimal code look like, what is it good at, and what should you watch out for. Code is deliberately minimal and uses a placeholder MODEL; check each project’s documentation for current model identifiers and options.

item.title: Agent Frameworks for Java, Kotlin and .NET
item.description:
Why JVM-native agents matter#

Most enterprise systems of record — banking cores, insurance platforms, ERP integrations — run on the JVM or .NET. Building agents in the same stack reuses existing security (Spring Security, OAuth), transactions, data access, messaging, observability and deployment pipelines, and keeps agents close to the services they call. Since 2025 the JVM has gained a real choice of agent frameworks.

item.title: Managed Agent Platforms and Low-Code Builders
item.description:
Simple definition#

A managed agent platform runs agents for you. You bring agent code written with almost any framework; the platform provides an isolated, scalable runtime, managed memory, identity for agents, a tool gateway that turns APIs into MCP tools, sandboxed browser and code tools, and observability — the operational layer most teams would otherwise build on Kubernetes.
